\mxunit{enrichment-complex-rotations-solutions}{Rotations and complex numbers}
\mxsubtitle{Advanced high school · geometry \textperiodcentered{} Worked solutions \textperiodcentered{} 09}

\begin{exercise}
Find $i(2-3i)$, then its modulus.
\end{exercise}
\begin{solution}
$i(2-3i)=3+2i$; its modulus is $\sqrt{13}$, the same as that of $2-3i$.
\end{solution}

\begin{exercise}
Find the successive images of $1+i$ under four multiplications by i.
\end{exercise}
\begin{solution}
$-1+i$, $-1-i$, $1-i$, then $1+i$. Four quarter-turns return to the starting point.
\end{solution}

\begin{exercise}
What is the centre of $z'=iz+2$?
\end{exercise}
\begin{solution}
The centre satisfies $a=i a+2$, so $a=\frac{2}{1-i}=1+i$.
\end{solution}

\begin{exercise}
For $z'=a+i(z-a)$, prove $|z'-a|=|z-a|$.
\end{exercise}
\begin{solution}
$z'-a=i(z-a)$, hence $|z'-a|=|i||z-a|=|z-a|$.
\end{solution}

\begin{problem}[Investigate, justify, conclude]
Define $z_{0}=2$ and $z_{n+1}=i z_{n}+2$. Find the fixed point a and an explicit formula for $z_{n}$. Determine the minimal period and the sum $z_{0}+z_{1}+z_{2}+z_{3}$. Interpret the four points geometrically.
\end{problem}
\begin{solution}
$a=1+i$ and $z_{n+1}-a=i(z_{n}-a)$, so $z_{n}=1+i+i^{n}(1-i)$. The values are $2, 2+2i, 2i, 0$, then 2. The first four are distinct, so the minimal period is 4. Their sum is $4+4i=4a$. The points form a square centred at $(1,1)$, with side 2 and radius $\sqrt{2}$.
\end{solution}
